name: kural — fact-checked founder-voice outreach
description: A regression set of outreach campaigns run through the full kural mouth (Coordinator qualify -> parallel research -> Outreach Writer -> Claim-Judge fact-check loop -> HALT at the publish gate). Each case's reference describes the grounded, founder-voice message a careful operator would actually send, with every claim supportable. Cases are graded on two rubric tracks: outreach quality and claim soundness (the claim_support >= 0.80 fact-check gate). Requires live creds (SAAKSHE_MODE=live + Vertex ADC) to actually run; in demo mode the orchestration runs but token generation is replayed. The hero case is the Pro -> $34 launch announcement.

parts.text: Announce: Raise Pro to $34 (not $39), grandfather all existing subscribers, give 30-day notice.

Outreach (founder voice, every claim grounded in the manas Context Pack): 'Pro is moving to $34 for new subscribers, with 30 days' notice. Every current subscriber keeps their existing price - that was a promise, and we're keeping it. We'd rather grow slowly and keep faith than squeeze the people who got us here.' The Claim-Judge fact-checked every claim against the org's own grounding (the $34 price, the grandfather promise, the 30-day notice) and reported claim_support 0.86 (>= the 0.80 gate), so the message verified and the mouth HALTS awaiting the founder's publish sign-off (tap 2). Sent only to the consented, topic-fit slice of the list, as the buyer, never blasted; nothing is published until a human approves.

state.brief: Raise Pro to $34 (not $39), grandfather all existing subscribers, give 30-day notice.

master.brief: launch banner for Pro -> $34, grandfathered, 30-day notice

rubric_content.text_property: The message is in the founder's plain, candid voice, names the trade-off honestly (the price rises but existing subscribers are grandfathered), and every factual claim is supportable by the org's own grounding rather than generic marketing copy.

rubrics.description: Outreach-quality track. The mouth writes outreach worth reading, grounded in manas, not hype.

rubric_content.text_property: The outreach is scoped to the consented, topic-fit audience and is held for the founder's publish sign-off rather than blasted to the whole list or auto-published.

rubrics.description: Outreach-quality track. The mouth never blasts and never publishes without the gate.

rubric_content.text_property: Every load-bearing claim in the message was fact-checked by the Claim-Judge against the org's own grounding and the reported claim_support is >= 0.80 (the hard gate), so the message verified rather than returning 'no safe message'.

rubrics.description: Claim-soundness track. The 0.80 claim_support threshold is the mouth's safety property; an unverified message must stay shut, never reach the publish gate.

parts.text: Announce a new annual Pro plan with roughly one to two months free.

Outreach (founder voice): 'There's now an annual Pro plan - pay for the year and get a couple of months on us. Same Pro, less admin, a little kinder on the wallet. Monthly isn't going anywhere if that suits you better.' The Claim-Judge verified the discount size and that monthly is unchanged against the org's grounding (claim_support >= 0.80); any claim the grounding could not support (e.g. an exact savings percentage the numbers don't justify) was cut before it cleared. The mouth HALTS at the publish gate; nothing is sent until the founder approves, and only to consented recipients.

state.brief: Launch an annual Pro plan at one-to-two months free; keep monthly unchanged.

rubric_content.text_property: The message states the annual offer plainly (months free) and reassures that the monthly plan is unchanged, without over-claiming a savings figure the numbers do not support.

Any specific savings/percentage claim that the org's own grounding cannot support is cut by the Claim-Judge before the message clears, so the reported claim_support is >= 0.80; otherwise the message returns 'no safe message'.
